editorial:
Imagine moving into a cool new loft in Los Angeles, only to find out your neighbors are hiding some pretty dark secrets. You follow Jessica as she settles into The Dante, a building that feels welcoming at first but quickly turns into a nightmare. She starts seeing people die in awful ways, and it becomes clear that something evil is happening on the eighth floor. Luckily, she meets Evan, who is played by the musician Doom. He helps her dig into the history of the place, and together they try to figure out why these deaths are happening and why Jessica was drawn to this specific building in the first place.

What makes this a fun ride is how it mixes a spooky mystery with some real tension. The acting is solid, and the twists keep you guessing until the very end. While some of the special effects feel a bit dated, the story moves quickly enough that you won't really mind. If you love low-budget horror with a strange plot, you should definitely check this out. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you want the best picture quality, try to find a 4K Blu-ray to add to your physical collection.
endingExplained: You find out that Jessica is actually part of a dark cycle involving a cult. The residents of the building are trapped in a loop of death and rebirth. In the final scenes, it is revealed that Jessica has been here before. The twist is that the deaths are sacrifices meant to keep a powerful force happy. Jessica and Evan try to break the cycle, but the ending leaves you wondering if the horror truly stopped.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves weird apartment mysteries and supernatural twists.
